Network Motif Analysis

Source: R/motifs-api.R
motifs.Rd

Classifies the node triples of a network into the 16 directed MAN triad types and tests their frequencies against a permutation null. The function has two modes.

  • In census mode (named_nodes = FALSE, the default), the result counts the triads of each MAN type. Nodes are exchangeable.

  • In instance mode (named_nodes = TRUE, or subgraphs()), the result lists the node triples that form each type.

Usage

motifs(
  x,
  named_nodes = FALSE,
  actor = NULL,
  window = NULL,
  window_type = c("rolling", "tumbling"),
  pattern = c("triangle", "network", "closed", "all"),
  include = NULL,
  exclude = NULL,
  significance = TRUE,
  n_perm = 1000L,
  cores = 1L,
  min_count = if (named_nodes) 2L else NULL,
  edge_method = c("any", "expected", "percent"),
  edge_threshold = 1.5,
  min_transitions = if (named_nodes) 3 else 5,
  top = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  family = c("observed", "all"),
  p_adjust = "none",
  strict = TRUE,
  count_repeats = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'cograph_motif_result'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  ...,
  what = c("results", "types"),
  significant = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

Input data: a tna object, cograph_network, matrix, igraph object or edge-list data frame. An edge list has the columns from and to (any case), an optional weight column weight or count (1 per row otherwise), the optional actor column described under actor, and an optional order column (timestamp, time, seq, step or order) that sorts the transitions within each actor before windowing. An edge list without from or to raises an error of class cograph_bad_edgelist. For as.data.frame(), a cograph_motif_result object returned by motifs() or subgraphs().

named_nodes

Logical. If FALSE (default), the MAN type census is computed. If TRUE, the individual node triples are listed. subgraphs() sets this to TRUE.

actor

Character. Name of the edge-list column that identifies the units. If NULL (default), the first column named session_id, session, actor, user, participant, individual or id (in that order, ignoring case) is used. Without such a column the analysis is aggregate.

window

Numeric. Window size for edge-list input. Each actor's transitions are cut into windows of this many transitions, and every window is analysed as one unit (individual level). window needs an actor column; without one it raises an error of class cograph_window_needs_actor. NULL (default) applies no windowing.

window_type

Character. "rolling" (default) windows start at every transition and overlap; "tumbling" windows are consecutive and do not overlap. Used only when window is set.

pattern

Which MAN triad types to include in the analysis:

"triangle"

(default) The 7 closed triangle types 030C, 030T, 120C, 120D, 120U, 210 and 300.

"network"

All types except 003 (empty), 012 (single edge) and 021C (chain).

"closed"

The same 7 closed types as "triangle": every pair of the three nodes is linked.

"all"

All 16 MAN types.

include

Character vector of MAN types to keep. When supplied, pattern and exclude are ignored, and the result records the pattern as "custom".

exclude

Character vector of MAN types to drop in addition to those removed by pattern.

significance

Logical. If TRUE (default), a permutation significance test is run. In instance mode the test requires individual data, and for aggregate input it is skipped with a warning.

n_perm

Number of permutations for significance. When significance = TRUE, must be a whole number of at least 2. Default 1000.

cores

Number of worker processes for the permutation null. Default 1 runs serially and draws all replicates from a single RNG stream. cores > 1 gives each replicate its own L'Ecuyer-CMRG stream, so the result depends on seed alone and is the same for every worker count. The serial and parallel streams differ, so a serial run and a parallel run with the same seed give different p-values. Forking is used where available, and Windows uses a PSOCK cluster. Only the individual-level census null is parallelized. Values above parallel::detectCores() are capped with a cograph_cores_capped warning.

min_count

Inclusive minimum count for a row to be kept. In census mode it filters the count column, the number of triads of each MAN type. In instance mode it filters the observed column. At individual level this is the number of units showing the triad, and at aggregate level it is the weighted edge mass of the triad (the sum of its 6 directed edge weights). Default 2 in instance mode, since at individual level a pattern seen in a single unit cannot recur, and NULL (no filter) in census mode. At aggregate level the threshold applies to the edge weight mass, so for probability matrices lower it (for example min_count = 1 or NULL).

edge_method

Method for determining edge presence: "any" (default; any positive edge), "expected" (ratio of the observed weight to the weight expected from the row and column totals), or "percent" (edge weight divided by the six-edge triad total).

edge_threshold

Threshold for "expected" or "percent" methods. For "expected", 1.5 means 50 percent above expected. For "percent", values at or below 1 are proportions and values above 1 are percentages. Default 1.5.

min_transitions

Minimum total edge weight for a unit to be included, counted after self-loops are removed unless count_repeats = TRUE. Default 3 in instance mode, the fewest transitions that can form a closed triad (030C and 030T have three edges), and 5 in census mode. At aggregate level the network is the only unit, so a network whose weights sum to less than this value gives NULL; for a probability matrix set min_transitions = 0.

top

Integer or NULL. Only the first top rows of the results are kept. NULL (default) keeps all rows.

seed

Random seed. Default NULL. When supplied, the caller's RNG state is restored on exit.

family

Which rows the instance-mode significance test covers. "observed" (default) tests the triple-type rows observed in at least min_count units. "all" tests every node triple crossed with every retained MAN type, including combinations no unit shows, and min_count then filters only the rows returned. Testing only observed rows selects on the outcome: a rare configuration enters the test only when it happens to occur, which inflates the false-positive rate well above the nominal level. "all" keeps it at or below the nominal level. The full family has choose(n_states, 3) rows per retained labelled pattern with strict = TRUE (for example six for 030T, two for 030C and one for 300), or per retained MAN type with strict = FALSE, so the permutation null grows accordingly. Ignored in census mode and without individual-level significance.

p_adjust

Multiplicity correction applied to the p-values of every tested row, one of p.adjust.methods. Default "none". The adjusted values are returned in p_adj and sig is p_adj < 0.05. With family = "all" the adjustment covers the full family before min_count is applied. Plot colours and stars follow p_adj, so they match sig.

strict

Logical. In instance mode, whether a row is one labelled pattern of a triple (TRUE, default) or one MAN type of a triple (FALSE). A MAN type fixes the shape of a triad but not which node plays which role: the cycles A to B to C to A and A to C to B to A are both 030C. With strict = TRUE the two are separate rows, a unit counts toward a row only when the triple shows exactly that set of arrows, and the null counts the same exact pattern. With strict = FALSE rows pool every labelled pattern of the type and pattern reports the most frequent one. Ignored in census mode.

count_repeats

Logical. Whether repeated codes (self-transitions such as A to A) count as transitions. Default FALSE: repeats are removed before anything else, so only transitions between different codes decide which units are analysed and enter the permutation null. With TRUE, repeats count toward min_transitions (a unit coded A, A, A, B, C has four transitions instead of two) and are shuffled with the other transitions in the null, which treats repeated codes as distinct events whose order is random. The null then also reflects how often units repeat: units that repeat a lot have fewer ties between different codes than their shuffles, which raises the number of dense triads the null expects. Observed triads never contain a repeat in either case, because a triad is made of ties between three different nodes.

row.names, optional

Standard as.data.frame arguments. row.names replaces the default row names; optional is ignored.

...

Unused.

what

Which table as.data.frame() returns, either "results" (default) or "types". The Value section lists the columns of each.

significant

Logical. When TRUE, as.data.frame() keeps only the rows whose sig flag is TRUE. It applies to what = "results" and needs a result computed with significance = TRUE; otherwise a cograph_no_significance error is raised. Default FALSE.

Value

A cograph_motif_result object, or NULL with a message when no motif passes the filters. The object is a list with the elements below.

results

Data frame of results. In census mode it has one row per retained, observed MAN type and the columns type and count. In instance mode it has one row per node triple and labelled pattern (strict = TRUE) or per node triple and MAN type (strict = FALSE), with the columns triad, node1, node2, node3, type, observed, pattern, pattern_n and pattern_code. At individual level, observed is the number of units in which the triple shows that pattern (or type), so one triple can occupy several rows. pattern is the labelled edge set of the row (for example "A -> B, B <-> C"). With strict = FALSE a row pools patterns that differ in direction, so pattern is the most frequent of them and pattern_n the number of units showing it; at individual level with strict = TRUE pattern_n equals observed. pattern_code is the same edge set as a six-bit code in node1, node2, node3 order (1: node1 to node2, 2: node2 to node1, 4: node1 to node3, 8: node3 to node1, 16: node2 to node3, 32: node3 to node2). Modal ties go to the smallest code. Rows that no unit shows (family = "all") have observed = 0 and pattern_n = 0; their pattern is the row's own pattern when strict = TRUE and missing otherwise. At aggregate level pattern_n is 1. With significance = TRUE, the columns expected (null mean), z, p, p_adj and sig are added, unrounded, and the rows are sorted by decreasing absolute z-score. Otherwise the rows are sorted by decreasing count. Census results carry expected, z, p, p_adj and sig in the same way.

type_summary

Named table of counts per MAN type, sorted in decreasing order. In census mode it holds the count column. In instance mode it holds the number of result rows of each type: node triple and labelled pattern with strict = TRUE, node triple and type with strict = FALSE.

level

"individual" when the input carried per-unit data, otherwise "aggregate".

named_nodes

The value of the named_nodes argument.

n_units

Number of units analyzed: the units whose transition total (loop-free unless count_repeats = TRUE) reaches min_transitions. 1 at aggregate level.

n_units_total

Number of units supplied, before the min_transitions filter.

params

List of the analysis settings: labels, n_states, pattern ("custom" when include is used), include, edge_method, edge_threshold, significance, n_perm, min_count, min_transitions, count_repeats, family, p_adjust, strict, window, window_type and actor (the actor column used, or NULL at aggregate level).

as.data.frame() returns one of these tables as a plain data frame. With what = "results" (default) it returns the results table described above. With what = "types" it returns one row per MAN type with columns type and count, where count is the number of triads of that type in a census or the number of result rows of that type in instance mode (see type_summary).

Details

The input type and the analysis level are detected automatically. Inputs that carry per-unit data are analyzed per unit. These are tna objects, networks that store sequence data (such as as_cograph() of a tna or a network from Nestimate::build_network()), and edge lists (or networks built from edge lists) with an actor column. Matrices, igraph objects and other networks are analyzed as one aggregate network. The adjacency is always classified as directed. The four-class undirected census is computed by motif_census(..., directed = FALSE).

For aggregate inputs, significance is computed by motif_census() with its degree-preserving rewiring null on the simple loop-free graph. Individual weighted inputs use a directed stub-matching null. Each positive edge weight is converted to at least one integer stub, and target stubs are shuffled within each unit so that its integer in- and out-margins are preserved. The resulting multigraph, which may contain loops or parallel edges, is classified through its simple loop-free triad projection. Self-loops are removed before counting. They are also removed before the null is constructed, unless count_repeats = TRUE, in which case they are shuffled with the other transitions.

With edge_method = "percent", edge presence is computed within each node triple. The weight of an edge is divided by the sum of the six possible directed edge weights of that triple. A threshold above 1 is read as a percentage (1.5 means 1.5 percent), and a threshold at or below 1 is read as a proportion.

With an edge_method other than "any", the significance test has limits. For aggregate census input, the observed counts use the threshold while the null tests the unthresholded network, and a warning is raised. For individual census input, the threshold is reapplied to each stub-null replicate. For individual instance input, the null classifies raw stub presence and does not reapply edge_method or edge_threshold. In every weighted individual null, a positive fractional weight keeps at least one stub. This preserves the support but can change the weight scale used by "percent" and "expected". Descriptive results with significance = FALSE or edge_method = "any" are unaffected.

Printing and plotting

Printing the result shows the analysis settings, the MAN type distribution and the first 20 rows of the results table. as.data.frame() returns the tidy tables. plot() on the result is documented in plot-results.

See also

subgraphs(), motif_census(), extract_motifs()

Other motifs: extract_motifs(), extract_triads(), get_edge_list(), motif_census(), subgraphs(), triad_census()

Examples

census <- motifs(regulation_net, significance = FALSE)
as.data.frame(census, what = "types")
#>   type count
#> 1 030T    11
#> 2 120C     3
#> 3 030C     2
#> 4 120D     2
#> 5 120U     1
